composition.observation: At t=0.8 the shafts sit left and the turtle sits on the right third at mid-height, which balances, but the lower 40% of frame is near-black with concentric ripple rings that read as a second water surface and pull the eye down. At t=3.2 the turtle is right of centre heading right, nose about 370 px from the frame edge, with a large empty dark area behind it on the left; it is swimming out of frame. At t=5.4 five hard-rimmed grey discs are the brightest shapes and two of them overlap the turtle's shell and flipper, so the eye goes to the discs before the subject.
composition.delta: Plate 1 hangs a bright rippled surface ceiling across the top quarter and lets the turtle sit as a small silhouette in readable mid-water. Plate 2 centres the turtle against a lit caustic field. Plate 3 keeps the blurred turtle as the anchor, with bokeh as a secondary layer of varied, mostly small discs. The render has no surface ceiling, a dead bottom band, no lead room at the hero beat, and bokeh that competes with the turtle.
composition.correction: At t=0.8 replace the bottom ripple rings with open blue water that falls off gradually, and put a bright rippled surface band across the top 20-25% of frame. At t=3.2 place the turtle on the left third with its head toward frame right, so it has about 55% of frame width of lead room. At t=5.4 keep the largest near-lens discs off the shell (frame edges and corners), and make most discs small (20-60 px) with only one or two large ones.

lighting.observation: At t=0.8 four or five near-parallel white shafts fall from the top edge at about x=500-750 and fade by about 65% of frame height. They are close in width and spread little. There is no surface the light comes through: the top is an even cobalt glow with soft wisps. At t=3.2 the frame is nearly black, with mean L* around 6. The shafts are faint grey vertical bars that look pasted over the image, and the only bright marks are thin teal glowing threads in mid-water. A grey diagonal band crosses the shell instead of a caustic net, there is no floor and no contact shadow, and the shell's top and its flank do not separate into lit and shadowed sides. At t=5.4 the frame is again underexposed, and the discs are lit uniformly grey instead of by the shafts.
lighting.delta: Plate 1 has a bright refracting surface feeding broad soft volumetric columns into lighter blue depth. Plate 2 has a high-contrast cyan caustic web (p05-p95 about 50 L*) with the turtle lit pale on top. Plate 3 keeps that bright cyan background through the defocus. The render is at roughly a third of the plates' exposure and tonal range at 3.2 and 5.4. At 0.8 its brightness falls off the wrong way: bright at the top and black at the bottom, where the plate has a dark band under the surface and lighter water below it.
lighting.correction: Fan 6-8 shafts of irregular width (some 2-4x wider than others) out from one point above frame top-left, running toward lower right. Make them brightest just under a visible rippled surface and gone by the lower third. Give them a soft scattering halo, not hard-edged bars. At t=3.2 raise the exposure so the water reads as mid cobalt. Put a visible sand floor under the turtle with a sharp bright caustic net, and the same net softer and animated across the shell. Add a soft contact shadow on the sand offset down-right. Light the top of the shell about 4x brighter than its flank. At t=5.4 keep the background as bright as at 3.2 and only defocus it.

materials.observation: The shell is a flat brown ellipse. Down its spine runs a chain of five identical outlined hexagons, with straight radial lines and a thin rim ring around them. It reads as a graphic, not as raised keratin scutes, and has no lift at scute centres and no grazing specular rim. The flippers are flat grey leaves stamped with rows of small open circles. The head is a grey teardrop with circles on it. The flippers' trailing edges show no warm light coming through. There is no sand to judge. At t=5.4 the near-lens particles are grey discs with hard bright rims and a specular dot, so they read as soap or air bubbles, not out-of-focus snow. At t=0.8 marine snow is nearly absent; measured speckle density is 0.48, against a target of at least 1.
materials.delta: Plate 2's shell is a domed form with irregular polygonal scutes, dark seams and shading that follows the curvature, and its flippers carry a fine mottled texture. Plate 3's bokeh are soft-edged, cyan-tinted, low-contrast discs with pinpoint flakes among them. Plate 1 has dense small cyan particles throughout. The render's detail is about a quarter of the plates' at every keyframe.
materials.correction: Rebuild the carapace as irregular polygonal scutes: five vertebrals, four costal pairs, a ring of small marginals. Give each scute a slight dome by shading it lighter toward the key at upper left, with dark recessed seams and a thin specular rim on the edge the key grazes. Replace the circle stamps on the flippers and head with irregular dark-on-olive polygon mottling, and let the thin trailing edges glow warm amber where the key hits them from behind. Draw the near-lens bokeh as soft-edged discs (no bright rim, no specular dot) in pale cyan at low opacity. Add hundreds of 1-3 px snow flakes at three depths, brighter where they cross a shaft.

spatial.observation: At t=0.8 the shafts are seen side-on, as if the camera looks horizontally into open water. The turtle is seen from directly above, showing its full carapace, so the shot mixes two camera angles. At the bottom, concentric ripple rings make it read as if a water surface lies below the turtle. At t=3.2 the turtle floats over black space crossed by glowing teal threads. With no floor plane, contact shadow or perspective cue, nothing shows its size or its height above the bottom. At t=5.4 the defocus is uniform over the turtle and the background, which is plausible, but the bokeh discs are near-identical in brightness and edge quality across a 2x size range. That flattens the near-lens depth layers.
spatial.delta: Plate 1 reads unambiguously: surface above, turtle in profile in mid-water, depth falling away below. Plate 2 sets the turtle against a lit plane with rippled caustics receding toward a horizon. Plate 3 has bokeh at several sizes and opacities, plus sharp pinpoint flakes, which together give separate depth layers in front of the subject.
spatial.correction: Make the camera angle agree with what the frame shows. At t=0.8 show the turtle in three-quarter or side profile at a small scale, with the surface above it. Bring the top-down view in only as the camera tilts down during the crane. At t=3.2 lay a sand plane under the turtle in perspective: caustic cells get smaller and denser toward the top of frame, and a soft shadow sits a body-width away. At t=5.4 grade the near-lens discs: the largest are the faintest and softest, mid-size ones are a little brighter, and sharp 1-2 px flakes sit behind them.

color.observation: At t=0.8 the frame sits in the intended cobalt-to-navy range and the turtle is the only warm element. At t=3.2 and t=5.4 the grade collapses to near-black with a teal-grey cast: measured b* is about -4 and C* about 6-7, so the water reads as neutral dark, not deep blue. The teal of the threads is greener than the DESIGN palette's cyan. The shell keeps a muted amber across the shell, including on its shadowed side, so its warmth is not limited to where the key hits.
color.delta: The plates hold saturated cobalt and cyan on every keyframe (b* about -17 to -20, C* about 20). The render matches that only at 0.8 and drifts to desaturated teal-black by the hero beat, so the temperature does not hold across the shot.
color.correction: Carry the t=0.8 cobalt (#0b4f8a mid-water, #02121e only in the deepest shadow) through 3.2 and 5.4. Lift the shadows into navy instead of black. Shift the caustic and thread colour from teal-green toward cyan-white (#bfefff) for the highlights. On the shell, keep saturated amber (#9a6a3a) on the key-lit top only and let the flank and underside fall to a blue-grey, as red absorption would.

narrative.observation: The 0.8 still has a calm open-water feeling. By 3.2 the image reads as night or deep murk with neon-like threads, closer to a screensaver than sunlit shallows. At 5.4 the grey bubble discs make the rack focus look like air bubbles in a tank. A viewer would not describe sunlight, a caustic-lit sand floor, or marine snow in front of the lens.
narrative.delta: The plates carry quiet awe through light: a luminous surface, a turtle bathed in moving caustics, then soft cyan snow over a still-bright background. The render loses the sunlight after the first beat, and the turtle never meets the floor the brief describes.
narrative.correction: Keep sunlight present in every beat: the shafts and surface glow at 0.8, the sand floor and shell caustics at 3.2, and the same bright background behind the defocus at 5.4. Make the 5.4 foreground read as drifting organic flakes (irregular, soft, slowly tumbling, brighter in shafts), not round bubbles.

originality.observation: Several elements read as procedural or clip-art defaults. The turtle is drawn from primitives: an ellipse, a chain of five hexagons, flippers stamped with rows of circles. The background is generic glowing sine-wave threads and swirl wisps. The shafts are evenly spaced parallel bars. The bokeh is a set of identical translucent circles with a rim stroke.
originality.delta: The plates, though procedural stand-ins themselves, commit to specific choices: a refracting surface ceiling, a caustic web, irregular scute polygons, and bokeh of varied size and softness. The render's elements are less specific than the plates'.
originality.correction: Replace the hexagon chain and circle stamps with an irregular scute layout and mottled skin, drawn as a real green or loggerhead turtle would be. Replace the sine threads with a caustic net that sits on surfaces (sand, shell) and has a cell structure. Vary shaft width, spacing and intensity. Vary bokeh size, opacity and edge softness, with no rim strokes.

summary: Only the t=0.8 colour approaches the target. The hero and macro beats are underexposed, desaturated teal-black with no sand floor, caustics, contact shadow or credible shell material, and the turtle and bokeh read as clip-art primitives. Priorities: sunlit exposure and cobalt grade held through 3.2 and 5.4, a caustic-lit sand floor under a properly built shell, and soft varied marine-snow bokeh in place of grey bubbles. The plates show a grey-beige shell and a side-on turtle, while DESIGN asks for amber and the brief a crane-down view; I read that as stand-in plate limits rather than a direction conflict.
